# Cancellation and Refund Rules
Quillbrook Village Hall is a fictional organisation.

## 1. Scope
1.1 These rules were adopted on 12 February 2025.
1.2 They apply to accepted bookings under hall-bookings.md.
1.3 Cancellation requests must be submitted in writing.
1.4 The date the booking officer receives the request is the cancellation date.

## 2. Hirer cancellations
2.1 Cancellation at least 28 calendar days before the event gives a full refund.
2.2 Cancellation from 14 to 27 calendar days before the event gives a 50% refund.
2.3 Cancellation fewer than 14 calendar days before the event gives no refund.
2.4 The refund percentages apply to room, kitchen and equipment hire charges.
2.5 The £30 booking deposit is non-refundable in every hirer cancellation.
2.6 Refunds under 2.1 and 2.2 exclude the booking deposit.
2.7 An unpaid balance remains payable if the cancellation charge exceeds payments.

## 3. Hall cancellations
3.1 If the committee cancels an event, all payments are refunded.
3.2 This includes bookings cancelled for safety reasons under hall-safety.md.
3.3 The committee does not pay compensation for external costs.
3.4 The booking officer must notify the hirer as soon as reasonably possible.

## 4. Damage deposits
4.1 Damage deposits are returned within ten working days after the event.
4.2 Documented repair or additional cleaning costs may be deducted.
4.3 The hirer must receive an itemised statement of deductions.
4.4 Any disputed deduction is reviewed by two trustees.
4.5 An unused damage deposit is returned in full after hirer cancellation.

## 5. Refund processing
5.1 Refunds are made by bank transfer.
5.2 Approved refunds must be issued within 15 working days.
5.3 The treasurer records every refund in the payment ledger.
5.4 Refund approvals above £500 require two trustees.
5.5 Working days mean Monday to Friday, excluding public holidays.

# Booking Desk Quick Guide
Quillbrook Village Hall is a fictional organisation.

## 1. Using this guide
This sheet was last refreshed on 10 July 2026.
It is a convenience summary, not a governing document.
The governing documents and hall-changes.md always prevail.
Check the event and cancellation dates before quoting a price.

## 2. Rooms and prices
The Main Hall normally costs £28 an hour.
The Meeting Room costs £12 an hour.
The kitchen costs another £8 per booking.
Bookings normally last at least two hours per room.
Registered village groups generally get 25% off room hire.
Projectors cost £15 and portable speakers cost £10.
Display boards cost £5 per set.
Equipment and kitchen charges do not receive the group discount.

## 3. Booking and payment
Bookings can be requested up to a year ahead.
Allow at least three days before the event.
A booking is not accepted until confirmed in writing.
A £30 booking deposit is normally required.
The outstanding hire bill is generally due two weeks before the event.
Alcohol events also need a £100 damage deposit.

## 4. Opening and attendance
Monday to Thursday events now finish by 21:30.
Friday and Saturday events may run until 23:00.
Sunday events finish by 21:00.
The Main Hall holds up to 90 people.
The Meeting Room holds up to 24 people.
Combined events are limited to 100 people in the building.

## 5. Music and cancellations
Friday and Saturday amplified music stops at 21:30.
Music stops by 21:00 on other days.
Early cancellation may qualify for a full or partial refund.
Mid-range cancellations now generally receive 25% rather than 50%.
The booking deposit is normally kept when a hirer cancels.

## 6. Questions to refer
Check hall-refunds.md before promising any repayment.
Refer safety issues immediately to a trustee.
Do not settle disputed damage charges at the booking desk.

content.text:
**You get 50% of your room, kitchen and equipment hire charges back. The £30 booking deposit is not refunded.**

- **Notice period:** Your cancellation reached the booking officer on 29 May 2026, which is 17 calendar days before the 15 June event. That falls in the 14 to 27 day band (hall-refunds.md §2.2).
- **Why 50% and not 25%:** The committee cut that band's refund to 25%, but only from 1 June 2026. The controlling date is when the booking officer receives the cancellation (hall-changes.md §6.3). Yours arrived on 29 May, before the change took effect, so the original 50% applies.
- **Quick guide:** The Booking Desk Quick Guide says mid-range cancellations "generally receive 25%". That is a summary, and it defers to the governing rules and the changes register, so it doesn't apply to you.
- **Deposit:** The £30 booking deposit is non-refundable in every hirer cancellation (§2.5). The 50% refund also excludes it (§2.6), and the change register keeps that exclusion (§6.4).
- **Unpaid balance:** If the cancellation charge is more than what you've already paid, you still owe the difference (§2.7).
- **Damage deposit:** If you paid one, for example for an alcohol event, an unused damage deposit is returned in full after a hirer cancellation (§4.5).
- **Timing:** Approved refunds must be issued by bank transfer within 15 working days (§5.1–5.2).
